This one particular person should have a split $25 + $52 =$77 but the app was showing the person owing me around $96.32. Almost Perfect — I loved everything about this app until I realized that it was NOT calculating the final figure correctly. If two people take a trip and person A pays $100 and person B pays $50, the app says person B owes person A $50. That is not correct. Once the balance of $50 is paid, person A has paid $50 and person B has paid $100. The app should be taking $100-$50=$50.00 and dividing that total in half. Half of $50 is $25. That is what person B owes. Now both parties have paid $75. The app is doing the math wrong and one of the parties is getting screwed. Please fix it, so it can be worthy of the 5 stars people are giving it. It gets more complicated when you add more people. Please

The person “C” needs to only pay the person “A” for the insurance…..but the app calculates that the person “C” needs to pay the person “A” for the gasoline even if he is not added to the group, and on the other hand shows that the person “C” only needs to pay for insurance some small amount that is not realistic to the person “A” So already by adding first 2 expenses, the app totally miscalculates everything. Once Great, Now a Disappointment — I had been a loyal Tricount user for years, relying on it to manage shared expenses with my flatmates and for budgeting during both big and small trips. It was a simple yet effective tool that made splitting bills hassle-free. I even subscribed to the paid version before its acquisition because it genuinely added value. Unfortunately, since the acquisition, the app has gone downhill. The user interface has become unappealing, key features have been removed, such as charts, export/download functionality, and web app access and overall usability has declined. The lack of web access is particularly frustrating, as adding expenses via a phone can often be tedious, making the web version a far quicker option. More recently, I found that I couldn’t even generate individual reminders to settle bills, being forced instead into an incomplete bank account integration that still claims the feature is “coming soon.” At this point, the app no longer meets my needs, so I’ve made the switch to Splitwise. While it costs more than Tricount’s old pricing, I don’t mind paying for a service that actually works as intended. It’s disappointing to see such a useful app lose its edge, but it’s time to say goodbye. Tricount was great once, but not anymore.

Key features that need to be brought back: The ability to Check/Uncheck all users while adding an expense. An option to view only my expenses for better tracking. A new feature that could be beneficial: Once an expense is locked or closed, no further edits or additions should be allowed to maintain transparency. Accesibilidad con VoiceOver — La aplicación Tricount siempre me ha parecido un referente en accesibilidad, especialmente para quienes utilizamos VoiceOver en iPhone. Por eso me ha sorprendido que, tras las dos últimas actualizaciones, varios elementos importantes hayan dejado de ser accesibles. En concreto, los botones “Nuevo Tricount” y “Añadir gasto” no son correctamente reconocidos por VoiceOver, lo que dificulta realizar acciones básicas dentro de la aplicación. Es una pena porque Tricount ha destacado durante años por ofrecer una experiencia muy cuidada para todos los usuarios, incluidos aquellos con discapacidad visual. Espero que este problema pueda corregirse en una próxima actualización para que la aplicación vuelva a alcanzar el excelente nivel de accesibilidad que siempre ha tenido. Muchas gracias por vuestro trabajo y por tener en cuenta este comentario.

Factor 3=1 En lugar de repartir los gastos a partes iguales en este caso la familia 1 pagaría más ya que son más miembros. De verdad que con esta pequeña modificación sería perfecta. Entiendo que el propósito es la simplificación sin embargo deberíamos de poder ver de donde sale esa simplificación. Esto no aparece tampoco en algún reporte que se pueda exportar… así que este es el gran punto a mejorar para esta app Siguientes pasos: Recientemente la app anunció que van a reemplazar esta app por otra nueva y mejor, y te pide que te registres… a la hora de hacerlo me encuentro con que actualmente SOLO está disponible para países en el área económica europea… so… perdieron un cliente entusiasmado (o tal vez muchos). Paying, but ready to leave — I have used Splitwise since the days when it was free. I’m now getting ready to find an alternative. Two things bring me to this. First, after each scan receipt, I’m forced to watch a robot play’s arms while Splitwise uploads the receipt somewhere. This is not entertaining. This delays the next entry, making my time to enter multiple receipts longer than necessary. Second, Splitwise refuses to display my outstanding indebtedness the way I want. It is not uncommon for someone to give me an old receipt or for me to find an old receipt. Yes, I can enter those and enter the date of the receipt or the charge. Yes, Splitwise will update the balance(s) owed. However, Splitwise refuses to show me all of the receipts or entries that are associated with that outstanding balance. Splitwise will only show me receipts or entries month by month. This is unsatisfactory. For example, in January 2026 I was given a bag with receipts dating from January 26, back to July 2025. As I enter those in to Splitwise, including the date of the receipt or expense, Splitwise updates the outstanding balance. However, I cannot show anyone which receipts or entered expenses are associated with that outstanding balance. I can show them all of the receipts or expenses for January 2026, December 2025, November 2025, October 2025, September 2025, August 2025, and July 2025, but that is not useful. I can show them the recently entered receipts and expenses, but Splitwise displays the date each was _entered_, not the date of the expense or receipt. Surely it is reasonable to expect that Splitwise will show not only the balance(s), but also the receipts or expenses and dates associated with the receipt/expense.

Receipt Quality — I’ve been using Splitwise for years, and I honestly can’t understand how the receipt-image quality problem still isn’t fixed. This issue has been reported since 2015, yet the app still aggressively compresses every uploaded receipt into unusable low-resolution garbage. I regularly compress images for web and professional use, and nothing I do produces results this bad. This is on Splitwise, not on the user. What makes it unacceptable is the price. Charging 40 CAD per year for a subscription, while failing to solve a decade-old basic feature, is extremely disappointing. If it were a one-time 40 CAD purchase, maybe. But every single year for this quality? No, thank you. To make things worse, the app still doesn’t offer a simple download option for receipts you already uploaded. How is that missing in 2025? At this point I’m genuinely considering building my own Splitwise alternative using AI, because the core functionality I need — clear receipts and the ability to download them — is missing. Splitwise can do better, and given the subscription model, it absolutely should.

Muy recomendable — Llevo usando Splitwise desde hace tiempo y me parece una de esas aplicaciones que realmente simplifican la vida. Es perfecta para viajes, cenas, vacaciones, compartir piso o cualquier situación en la que varias personas tienen gastos en común. Lo que más me gusta es que calcula automáticamente quién debe a quién, evitando cuentas interminables y conversaciones incómodas. La interfaz es muy intuitiva, permite dividir los gastos de muchas formas (a partes iguales, por porcentajes o importes personalizados) y llevar un control claro de todos los movimientos. Además, tener el historial de gastos siempre disponible evita malentendidos y hace que todo sea mucho más transparente. Si compartes gastos con frecuencia, es una aplicación prácticamente imprescindible. Muy recomendable.

Me encanta — Splitwise es una aplicación muy útil para gestionar deudas y gastos compartidos de forma sencilla y transparente. Resulta especialmente práctica para familias, incluso para llevar cuentas con hijos, ya sea para pagas, gastos comunes, adelantos o actividades compartidas. La app permite registrar quién paga cada cosa y cómo se reparte el gasto, mostrando en todo momento quién debe a quién y cuánto. Esto ayuda a evitar confusiones, discusiones y olvidos, y favorece una relación más clara y responsable con el dinero, algo muy educativo cuando se usa con niños y adolescentes. Entre sus puntos fuertes destacan la facilidad de uso, la visualización clara de los saldos y la posibilidad de crear grupos familiares. Además, está disponible en móvil y web, por lo que todos pueden consultar las cuentas cuando lo necesiten. Como aspecto a tener en cuenta, la versión gratuita tiene algunas limitaciones y publicidad, aunque para un uso familiar básico suele ser suficiente. Conclusión: Splitwise es una herramienta práctica y eficaz para organizar gastos y deudas en familia, ideal para fomentar la responsabilidad económica y mantener las cuentas claras sin complicaciones.

Reevaluación de Splitwise: Impacto del Modelo de Pago — Splitwise era una aplicación de referencia para gestionar gastos compartidos, facilitando el seguimiento y la división de costos con amigos y familiares. Sin embargo, el reciente cambio a un modelo de pago ha disminuido significativamente su utilidad para mí. La introducción de tarifas de suscripción para características que antes eran gratuitas me ha hecho reconsiderar el valor de la aplicación en mi conjunto de herramientas de finanzas personales. Aunque entiendo la necesidad de que las aplicaciones generen ingresos, este movimiento ha hecho que Splitwise sea menos accesible y me ha obligado a buscar soluciones alternativas que ofrezcan funcionalidades similares sin el costo adicional. Es lamentable ver cómo una herramienta tan práctica y fácil de usar se vuelve menos atractiva debido a estos cambios.

Then it's very easy to assign amounts to individual people, allocating expenses separately for each person. TIP: To assign the cost of an item to people: 1. Select the person first (not the item). 2. Then select all items for which the person will pay some or all of the cost. 3. Select another person, and do the same. If multiple people are signed to the same item, the cost is automatically divided! The app allows you to add additional items, correct misinterpreted ones, enter any discounts, as well as specifying the amount of sales tax and the percent of tip. If the check is handwritten, or there is any other reason that you need to enter all the amounts yourself, you can skip the photo and OCR, and enter the numbers manually. It's all very easy, and the user interface is well done. I contacted technical support with a potential problem, and their responsiveness was excellent.

Then, the app added a 58 dollar tip and I have no idea where they came from even after investigating my receipt. A 20% tip on our bill (which we left) was only ~20 dollars. This app also does not let you edit the dollar amount of tax charged (in my case the app put it down as 0, which isn’t correct), which seems like a massive oversight. You should at least have the option to manually enter the amount of percentage of tax charged considering how bad the app is at itemizing. I am giving two stars, simply because the app DID itemize the actual items on my receipt correctly, with correct dollar amount and (close enough) names. With some manual override, I was about to get the bill within ~10 dollars of the actual amount paid - so in the end it can still be useful. This app has a lot of potential, it just needs a better algorithm at itemizing, and a manual override feature for the amount of tax paid.

Top tier splitting app — This is absolutely one of the best if not the best splitting app available. First- the most common activity on this kind of app is adding an expense on the go, so you want it to be quick and painless. Settle up by far has the fastest expense adding framework, because you can start by tapping the name of the person who paid. Seems like a small thing, but it makes a big difference in the field. Second- exporting transactions is not behind a paywall. Third- unlimited transactions not behind paywall. Fourth- default shares for groups and an advanced expense adding experience for things like meals where tax and tip might be separate from the item subtotal. This includes a calculator in the subtotal area as well. Overall- the app looks a little dated. But who cares. All the basic functionality is there, it’s the fastest to add an expense, and only appropriate functionality is behind the paywall (like categories, receipt storage, and recurring transactions).

Great app, very intuitive and well thought through. But — This is the best app for splitting expenses I found. It has a very slick interface, all required details are easily available and accessible. I wish it had 3 relatively small features that I proposed to the authors that could be implemented (had no negative or positive response from the authors so far). Ability to assign a fixed amount to a person(s) and exclude them from further sharing. Use case: a participant bought something completely different and their prices are fixed regarding the rest of the spending Ability to assign adjustments for sharing. Use case: in a restaurant, the entire bill is split evenly but one person ordered an expensive drink for himself and wants to exclude this amount from sharing, or a person didn’t order an expensive dessert and its share should be reduced by this amount Ability to create a paying group which is very natural in multi-family events (especially with children who could be accounted for differently). All calculations are as is but in the end, group spending and debts are combined. It makes regular accounting simple. No multipliers, all other accounting as described in 1) and 2) are still applicable on the individual level but the final settlement is natural The nice thing is that all these features could be introduced in a way that the old interface would work the same way without additional complexity for those who are not interested yet accommodating more complex use cases. I hope developers would listen to this proposals, it doesn’t look too complex and should not change the existing API too much

The Best Bill Splitting App — Splid is a game-changer for anyone who frequently finds themselves splitting bills with friends, family, or colleagues. Whether you’re on a group trip, dining out, or sharing expenses with roommates, this app makes the process effortless and fair. **User-Friendly Interface** The first thing you’ll notice about Splid is its clean and intuitive interface. It’s incredibly easy to set up a group, add expenses, and assign them to the relevant people. Even if you’re not tech-savvy, you’ll find navigating through the app a breeze. **Flexible Expense Tracking** Splid allows you to split bills in multiple ways—equally, by percentage, or custom amounts—catering to different group dynamics. You can add notes to each expense, which is great for remembering specific details. The app supports multiple currencies, making it ideal for international trips. **Offline Functionality** One of Splid's standout features is its ability to work offline. You don’t need a constant internet connection to manage your expenses, which is perfect when you’re traveling or in areas with poor connectivity. Once you’re back online, the app syncs everything automatically. **Seamless Settlement Process** When it’s time to settle up, Splid provides a clear breakdown of who owes whom, simplifying the payment process. You can also export the summary as a PDF or Excel file, making it easy to keep records or share with your group. **No Sign-Up Required** Another major plus is that Splid doesn’t require users to sign up for an account, which is a refreshing change from most apps. You can start using it right away without worrying about privacy concerns. **Conclusion** Splid is hands down the best bill-splitting app available on the App Store. Its combination of user-friendly design, flexibility, and offline functionality makes it a must-have tool for anyone who regularly shares expenses. If you’re tired of the hassle and awkwardness of splitting bills, Splid is the solution you’ve been looking for. Highly recommended!

Words can’t explain how kind and considerate this app developer is in making sure the customer is satisfied and the app gets the fixes it might need. Love Debty — This is exactly what I was looking for in a debt tracking app: it's very simple, very straightforward, very easy to use, attractive to look at, and while in general I don't like subscription-based software, I'll pay for a subscription if I think the software is really worth it, and Debty is. You can get a monthly subscription for $2.99/month or an annual one for $24.99/year; I saw the value of this software and went with the annual subscription. You don't have to create an account or log in, there are no ads, it doesn't want you to link your bank account or any of that nonsense...it tracks your debts (whether owed by you or to you) and their repayments, and that's it. I love it, and will continue to use it for as long as it runs on my devices. ♥️

I wish the rest of life was this easy. — If you have any debts owed by you or to you, you must getty Debty. I first downloaded a “competing” debt-tracker app that had five stars (from a total of 8 users) and found it unintuitive, a bit strange; I had to put forth some effort to figure out how to use it. Once I did, it was okay, but not ideal, so I went back to the App Store and grabbed Debty to give it a try, and it was exactly what I’d been looking for when I downloaded the first app: simple, straightforward, and 100% intuitive. By the time I’d entered my first debt I was sufficiently happy with the app to subscribe. And I’m not a fan of subscription-based software. But at the current price of $15.99 a year, and considering the quality and ease-of-use of the product, it was a no-brainer for me: I want to support this software and this developer. The Mac needs much more software like this, made with Apple (Computer)’s original design philosophy at its core: intuitivity (it’s a word *now*). Software that works the way humans expect it to, rather than forcing humans to work the way the software expects *them* to. If you’re looking for a simple (and intuitive) app to track your debts, this is it. 👍🏻

Good idea, with some needed improvements — This is an okay app that could be great. First and foremost, its analysis of a sample receipt produced A LOT of erroneous fields that needed to be deleted. This coupled with the app's inability to apply negative values for discount line items makes it not much quicker than calculating by hand. Furthermore, there must be a calculation error when splitting the bill since a quick sum of everyone's total was almost a dollar shy of the real total. Please fix these issues. Finally, the app's tip calculation is simplistic and incorporates the sales tax rather than only the subtotal. Sales tax is already a percentage of the subtotal and is often >10% in some locales. Therefore, tipping on the total rather than the subtotal inflates the the selected tip percentage by more than you’d think. I've been using “Tip Calculator +++” by Aaron Jubbal for years since it accounts for this. Including this functionality would make “IOU: Easily Split Your Tab” the perfect app! Looking forward to future versions!
